beats.headline: Asana reports 76x lower model cost and 5x speed in browser-agent tests
beats.summary: Asana ran the tests with GPT-6 Astra in Codex, weeks after OpenAI's Sep 29 GPT-6.1 Sol launch.

beats.headline: Report: Codex CLI defaults to GPT-6.1 Sol; price cut restated from 80% to 77%
beats.summary: Both posts come from one outlet, tech-insider.org; OpenAI has not confirmed the default or the figure.

open_questions: Does OpenAI confirm Codex CLI's default switch to GPT-6.1 Sol, and is the cut 80% or 77%?
Does Asana's 76x cost reduction reproduce outside its browser-agent tests?
How does GPT-6.1 Sol compare with Claude Opus 5.5 on cost per completed task?

status.detail: GPT-6.1 Sol has moved from launch to a customer cost claim and a reported Codex CLI default whose price cut is still unconfirmed (80%, then 77%).

editorial.take_for_builders: Treat the Codex CLI price cut as unconfirmed: rerun your coding and computer-use evals on GPT-6.1 Sol against your Astra baseline on cost per completed task, and check OpenAI's pricing page before changing any default model.
editorial.tldr: OpenAI는 9월 29일 GPT-6.1 Sol을 공개하며 코딩과 computer use에서 Astra에 가까운 성능을 Astra API 토큰 가격의 5분의 1에 제공한다고 내세웠습니다. 10월 9일 Asana는 테스트에서 자사 브라우저 agent가 76배 저렴하고 5배 빨라졌다고 밝혔습니다.
editorial.whats_new: A second tech-insider.org post now puts the reported Codex CLI default switch to GPT-6.1 Sol at 77% cheaper, down from 80% two days earlier; OpenAI has not confirmed either figure.
editorial.why_it_matters: GPT-6.1 Sol lowers the price of Astra-class coding and computer-use work, so routing and cost-per-task assumptions built on Astra pricing are out of date.
